mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate signals monetary tightening that raises discount rates for equity valuation, compressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS has increased over the prior 3 months, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 5.0% indicates labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE > 5.0%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous acceleration in inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%) and rising policy rates (FEDFUNDS > 0.5%) triggers aggressive monetary tightening that depresses equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of instances where CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5% and FEDFUNDS > 0.5%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
